tagline: Caracas's Caribbean gateway port, with the Los Roques archipelago and a resort coast on its doorstep.
summary: La Guaira is the main seaport of Venezuela's north-central coast and the historic maritime gateway to Caracas, a short mountain crossing inland. East of the port the Caraballeda and Naiguata resort coast lines the Caribbean, while ~80 nautical miles offshore lies the Los Roques archipelago, a national park of roughly 350 coral islands and one of the country's marquee destinations. Movement along the coast is road-bound and Los Roques is reached mainly by light aircraft, leaving the water under-used for scheduled passenger transport.

transit_planning: Coastal transport centres on the La Guaira port, the airport and the mountain highway to Caracas; scheduled passenger water services are undeveloped, and Los Roques access leans on light aircraft, leaving room for a marine tier.

competitive_landscape: There is no scheduled fast passenger-vessel service on the central coast; the resort coast is road-served and Los Roques is reached mainly by light aircraft, so a clean water tier opens coastal links and a marine alternative to the island air shuttle. Operating context is shaped by Venezuela's economic and sanctions environment.
seasonality: The central Caribbean coast is warm year-round with a drier season (roughly December-April) and a wetter, occasionally squally season mid-year; calm mornings favour coastal running and the ~80nm offshore leg is weather-windowed.
regulatory_note: Maritime affairs fall under Venezuela's national aquatic-and-port authority (INEA); passenger-vessel licensing, national-park rules for Los Roques, and the prevailing sanctions/political-risk context all frame any scheduled service.

precedents.why_it_matters: Shows durable premium demand for reaching a marquee archipelago that a marine express can serve.
Demonstrates concentrated gateway movement across a narrow coastal strip suited to water links.
